Subject: Draft: BCDR answers for WellSight (RTO/RPO, backups, failover)

Hi team — see draft answers below, pulled from our infra runbooks and last rehearsal notes. I kept the language concise for auditors; we can expand any item Alex asks for.

1) RTO / RPO (tiered):
- Critical (real-time inference endpoints impacting customer API traffic): RTO = 15 minutes (automated regional failover + traffic routing); RPO = <5 minutes (continuous replication + KV checkpointing).
- High (model management, control plane services): RTO = 60 minutes; RPO = 15 minutes (hourly snapshots + WAL shipping).
- Non-critical (reporting, batch jobs): RTO = 24 hours; RPO = 1 hour.

2) Backups & retention:
- Customer metadata (Postgres): continuous WAL archiving + daily snapshots retained 30 days; nightly incremental backups retained 90 days in object storage.
- Model artifacts and container images: immutable object storage with versioned keys; snapshots taken on model publish events and weekly full snapshots retained 365 days.
- KV caches / session state: ephemeral by design; we persist summaries and critical checkpoints to object storage every 5 minutes for stateful workflows.
- Backup storage: multi-zone replication within a region plus asynchronous cross-region replication to a secondary region within the same cloud provider.

3) Replication & regional failover:
- Architecture: active-active serving in two primary regions (us-west-2, us-east-1) with a warm-standby third region (us-central-1).
- Failover: automated via health checks and our routing layer (DNS + global load balancer). For targeted outages we trigger automated traffic shift to the healthy region; for severe incidents we follow the runbook to promote warm standby. Typical time to failover (automated): 5-20 minutes depending on session draining; manual promotion of warm-standby: ~60 minutes.

4) Testing / evidence:
- We run monthly smoke failover tests (partial) and quarterly full restore rehearsals. Last full rehearsal: 2027-02-10 (scope: full stack restore for a single region + validation of inference latency targets).
- Evidence available: restore playbook (attached), backup logs for Q1 2027 (attached ZIP with scrubbed customer identifiers), post-mortem/test reports in the SOC 2 evidence folder.

5) Stateful session recovery notes:
- We aim for transparent session recovery where possible; KV checkpointing reduces warmup time. Some transient session-level state (e.g., ephemeral local caches) will be lost and reconstructed; we document expected behaviors in the runbook so customers can design idempotent clients.

Attachments to include: redwood_bcdr_summary.pdf (one-page summary), restore_playbook.pdf (runbook excerpt), backup_logs_q1_2027.zip (sanitized logs).

Comments welcome — once Aditya confirms the technical bits I'll finalize wording for the customer.

Marissa
Senior SRE, Platform Reliability
Redwood Inference

Short answers (full detail attached):
- RTO/RPO: Tiered targets — Critical: RTO 15m / RPO <5m; High: RTO 1h / RPO 15m; Non-critical: RTO 24h / RPO 1h.
- Backups: DB WAL + daily snapshots; model artifacts versioned in object storage; KV checkpointing every 5 minutes. Retention: DB nightly increments 90 days; model snapshots 365 days.
- Failover: Active-active in two primary regions with warm standby; automated failover 5-20 minutes, manual promotion ~60 minutes.
- Tests: Monthly smoke tests, quarterly full restore; last full rehearsal 2027-02-10. Evidence: attached restore_playbook.pdf, backup_logs_q1_2027.zip, redwood_bcdr_summary.pdf.
